# Sum of intervals, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_add_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ that contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, with $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x + y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $y_l = y_{l0} + y_{l1}$, $y_u = y_{u0} + y_{u1}$, $z_l = z_{l0} + z_{l1}$, $z_u = z_{u0} + z_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X + Y` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | rounds; not `constexpr`: its code is where `KAIRN_ENCLOSURE_CODE` puts it |
| `X += Y` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | rounds; not `constexpr`: its code is where `KAIRN_ENCLOSURE_CODE` puts it |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $x + y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For bounded $X$ and $Y$ and a bounded $Z$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, x + y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $\ell - z_l \le A\,\lvert \ell\rvert + B$ and $z_u - h \le A\,\lvert h\rvert + B$, with the constants $A$ and $B$ below. A bound of $Z$ is the bound of the range exactly for the lower bound when $x_l + y_l = 0$, for the upper bound when $x_u + y_u = 0$. For nonempty operands, an infinite bound of the range is returned as such.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$ and $Y$, $Z$ is bounded when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 2}$. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 2}$ is $2^{1022}$ for `double`, $2^{126}$ for `float`.

The constants of the bound, from `gen/claims.json`: $A$ is `(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)*(1+unit(add_2_2))/(1-u)` and $B$ is `2*(1+u)^2*(1/2*up((1+u)^3)*eta+up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))+eta+(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)/(1-u)*tiny(add_2_2)`, where `up( )` is a constant as `T` rounds it up (the $E$, $G$, $H$ of a radius) and `unit( )`, `tiny( )` are the constants of the center's kernel; $N$ is the smallest normal number of `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| $A / u^2$ | $8.0000000000000091 \times 10^{0}$ | $8.0000048875823637 \times 10^{0}$ |
| $B / N$ | $2.0000000000000018 \times 10^{0}$ | $2.000000953674423 \times 10^{0}$ |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_add_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeInterval2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeInterval2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_add_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_add_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the directed sums of two limbs, an infinite or empty result selected (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_add_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_add_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_down_2_2`](add_down_2_2.md), [`add_up_2_2`](add_up_2_2.md).

```
# The sum of two intervals with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Two limbs"). The
# finite cores add_down_2_2 and add_up_2_2 give the bounds; a bound that a core does not return as
# a finite number (an unbounded operand, or an overflow inside the core) becomes the infinity on its
# side, which is always a bound; an empty operand gives the empty set. Tightness for bounded
# operands and a bounded result: each bound within A |v| + B of the bound v of the exact range, with
# the constants of the directed sums; a bound of the exact range that is zero is returned as zero
# (the rule of the zero sum of the cores). Bounded when the exact range is within a quarter of the
# overflow threshold.

(l0, l1) = add_down_2_2(xl0, xl1, yl0, yl1)
(h0, h1) = add_up_2_2(xu0, xu1, yu0, yu1)
al  = abs(l0)
fl  = lt(al, const inf)
ah  = abs(h0)
fh  = lt(ah, const inf)
mi  = neg(const inf)
a0  = select(fl, l0, mi)
a1  = select(fl, l1, 0)
b0  = select(fh, h0, const inf)
b1  = select(fh, h1, 0)
nx  = lt(xl0, const inf)
ny  = lt(yl0, const inf)
ne  = and(nx, ny)
zl0 = select(ne, a0, const inf)
zl1 = select(ne, a1, 0)
zu0 = select(ne, b0, mi)
zu1 = select(ne, b1, 0)
```
